Bug_Details: Duration APIs only work for DAYS or exact durations. Duration APIs only work for TemporalUnits with exact durations or ChronoUnit.DAYS. E.g., Duration.of(1, ChronoUnit.YEARS) is guaranteed to throw a DateTimeException.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where Duration.of() is used with an argument of a ChronoUnit which is not ChronoUnit.DAYS or a TemporalUnit with exact durations. This will throw a DateTimeException.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug() method with a ChronoUnit that is not DAYS or a TemporalUnit with exact durations. In this case, it uses ChronoUnit.YEARS, which is not supported by the Duration.of() method as per the bug rule.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the test passed successfully without throwing a DateTimeException. This suggests that the bug was not triggered in this test case, as the bug is expected to cause the method to throw a DateTimeException when using a TemporalUnit other than DAYS or an exact duration.
